headline: Sharan CK's all-round day trumps Rohith Bhardwaj's unbeaten 72
summary:
GSCC Bears beat Sunnyvale CC by six wickets with 28 balls to spare at Ortega Park, as Sharan CK's two-wicket over and quickfire 40 outweighed Rohith Bhardwaj's unbeaten 72.

Sent in after GSCC won the toss, Sunnyvale were 23 without loss after four overs before Abhilash Ramesh Venkata and Muneer Syed removed Ashok Kumar Venna and Bharadwaj Jagannath in successive overs. Rohith and Govardhan Mucharla rebuilt with a stand of 53, and a Rohith six in a 13-run 12th over took them to 80 for 2, but Sharan removed Govardhan and Pranav Jain in the space of three balls in the 13th. Only 28 runs came from overs 13 to 17, and Ankit Mishra was run out along the way.

Rohith batted through the innings, reaching his first NCCA T20 fifty off 51 balls in the 16th over. Sunnyvale found some late momentum, with 31 coming from the last three overs and Ravi Shankar hitting his first ball for six, to finish on 139 for 6.

Palanivel Purushothaman struck with his first legal ball of the chase, but Sharan hit Bilal Ahamad for a six and a four in a 15-run second over and made 40 off 24 before Arun Subramanian had him caught by Bilal in the ninth. Palanivel then took two wickets in two balls in the 13th, trapping Abhimanyu Karthik lbw for 26 off 13 and Prashant Krishnan next ball, and Ankit followed with five dots in a row in the 14th to finish with 3-0-10-0. That left GSCC needing 22 from 36 balls at 118 for 4, but Mazher Khan's unbeaten 49 steered them home in the 16th over.

Sunnyvale's bowlers also gave away 22 wides, about one in every six of GSCC's runs. Sharan was named player of the match.

standfirst: Sharan took 2 for 24 and hit 40 off 24 as GSCC Bears chased 140 with 28 balls to spare at Ortega Park
report:
Rohith Bhardwaj batted through all 20 overs for an unbeaten 72, his first fifty in NCCA T20 cricket, but Sunnyvale CC's season opener belonged to Sharan CK. GSCC Bears' all-rounder took two wickets in three balls to stall Sunnyvale's innings, then hit 40 off 24 at the top of the chase as GSCC won by six wickets with 28 balls to spare.

Sent in after GSCC won the toss, Sunnyvale were 23 without loss after four overs before Abhilash Ramesh Venkata and Muneer Syed removed Ashok Kumar Venna and Bharadwaj Jagannath in successive overs. Rohith and Govardhan Mucharla rebuilt with a stand of 53, and Rohith's six off Rohit Bhamidipati in a 13-run 12th over took them to 80 for 2.

Then came Sharan. With more than 4,000 NCCA T20 runs and 80 wickets behind him, he had Govardhan caught behind for 19 and bowled Pranav Jain two balls later. Only 28 runs came from overs 13 to 17, and Ankit Mishra was run out along the way. Rohith reached his fifty off 51 balls in the 16th over and Sunnyvale found some late momentum, taking 31 from the last three overs, with Ravi Shankar hitting his first ball for six. But 139 for 6 was some way short of the 160 that sides batting first average at Ortega Park.

Palanivel Purushothaman gave the defence the perfect start, having Rohit Bhamidipati caught behind by Govardhan with his first legal ball. Sharan hit back, taking Bilal Ahamad for a six and a four in a 15-run second over, but Palanivel, Bilal, Arun Subramanian and Ravi held GSCC to 63 for 1 after eight overs.

The ninth over swung the game back. Sharan hit Arun for six before Bilal caught him off the next ball, but Abhimanyu Karthik, who averages 36 in NCCA T20s, hit his first ball for six and the over cost 17. Palanivel struck back in the 13th, trapping Abhimanyu lbw for 26 off 13 and Prashant Krishnan with his next legal delivery, after Abhimanyu had taken him for 6, 4 and 4. Ankit followed with five dots in a row in the 14th, completing a spell of 3-0-10-0, and at 118 for 4 GSCC still needed 22 from 36 balls.

Mazher Khan, who finished 49 not out off 45, made sure there was no wobble. He took two fours off Palanivel in the 15th, and the winning runs came from three wides by Fnu Rajat in the 16th. Sunnyvale's bowlers sent down 22 wides in all, about one in every six of GSCC's runs.

toss: Sunnyvale CC won the toss and chose to bowl
headline: Rohith Bhardwaj's all-round day sets up nine-wicket win
summary:
Rohith Bhardwaj starred with bat and ball as Sunnyvale CC beat BMCC Masters by nine wickets at Ortega Park, chasing 154 with 19 balls to spare for their first win of the season.

Sunnyvale chose to bowl, and Palanivel Purushothaman struck in the first over, having BMCC's most experienced T20 batter, Prashant Kommireddi, caught behind by Govardhan Mucharla for 5. Karthik Manepalli took 18 off Avinash Pali in the second over, and he and Rahul Pendyala added 76 for the second wicket, and at 80 for 1 after nine overs BMCC were scoring at almost nine an over.

The game turned when Arun Subramanian and Rohith bowled eight overs in tandem for 43 runs and four wickets. Arun removed Rahul for 33 and Karthik for 43, while Rohith bowled the BMCC captain Gaurav Gosain and had Gokul Jayaraman caught, finishing with 2 for 20 from his four overs. Bilal Ahamad bowled Anand Vasudevan to leave BMCC 124 for 6, before Harish B's unbeaten 35 off 24, including 18 off the 19th over, lifted them to 153.

Rohith then took charge of the chase, hitting four fours in the fifth over as Sunnyvale reached 56 without loss after the powerplay. He brought up his fifty in the seventh over, his second in a week, and he and Govardhan had 100 on the board after 11 overs. Mahendar Madhavan's leg-spin removed Rohith for 70 off 48 balls, and BMCC conceded only 24 runs from overs 12 to 15 to leave Sunnyvale needing 30 off 30.

Bharadwaj Jagannath settled it in one over, taking Mahendar for 4, 6, 0, 6, 6 and 1, and finished the game with a six off Rajmohan Muthaiah. He ended 37 not out off 17, with Govardhan unbeaten on 36, and Rohith was named player of the match.
key: Rohith Bhardwaj: 70 off 48 (10 fours, 2 sixes) and 2/20 with 12 dot balls
Arun Subramanian: 2/23 with 11 dots, removing top scorer Karthik Manepalli (43) and Rahul Pendyala (33), plus a catch
Bharadwaj Jagannath: 37* off 17 with 4 sixes, including 23 off one over
Govardhan Mucharla: 36* and a 102-run opening stand, plus a catch behind the stumps
Bilal Ahamad: 1/27 in 4 overs plus a catch; Pranav Jain caught the top scorer
standfirst: Rohith took 2 for 20 and made 70 off 48 as Sunnyvale CC chased 154 with 19 balls to spare
report:
Rohith Bhardwaj had a hand in almost everything at Ortega Park on Saturday. He bowled four tidy overs for 20, then hit 70 off 48 balls at the top of the order as Sunnyvale CC beat BMCC Masters by nine wickets with 19 balls to spare. It was his second fifty in a week, and only the second of his NCCA T20 career. A week after losing to GSCC Bears, Sunnyvale have their first win of the season.

Sunnyvale chose to bowl on a ground where sides batting first average 160, and the call paid off in the first over. Palanivel Purushothaman had Prashant Kommireddi, BMCC's most experienced T20 batter with ten NCCA fifties, caught behind by Govardhan Mucharla for 5.

BMCC regrouped quickly. Karthik Manepalli took Avinash Pali for two sixes and a four in an 18-run second over, and Rahul Pendyala hit Ravi Shankar for a four and a six in the eighth. At 80 for 1 after nine overs, BMCC were scoring at almost nine an over.

The game turned on the eight overs Arun Subramanian and Rohith bowled in tandem from the tenth. Arun, better known for his miserly one-day off-spin, ended a 76-run stand when Rahul (33) was caught by Bilal Ahamad. Rohith bowled the BMCC captain Gaurav Gosain in the 13th, and Arun removed Karthik for 43, caught by Pranav Jain. Rohith then had Gokul Jayaraman caught by Arun with the first ball of the 17th. Those eight overs cost 43 runs for four wickets, and when Bilal bowled Anand Vasudevan in the next over, BMCC were 124 for 6.

Harish B lifted them to 153 with an unbeaten 35 off 24, his best NCCA T20 score, including 18 off Palanivel's 19th over. BMCC never got Anand Baskarababu, who averages 40 with the bat in T20s, to the crease.

Rohith set the tone for the chase in the fifth over, hitting Anand Vasudevan for four fours, and Sunnyvale had 56 without loss after the powerplay. He brought up his fifty in the seventh over while Govardhan kept rotating the strike, and the openers had 100 on the board after 11 overs.

BMCC's best spell followed. Mahendar Madhavan's leg-spin removed Rohith, caught by Prashant for 70 in the 12th over, and with Prashant's off-spin at the other end, overs 12 to 15 brought only 24 runs. Sunnyvale needed 30 off 30 balls.

Bharadwaj Jagannath settled it in one over, taking Mahendar for a four and three sixes in a 23-run 16th. He then finished the match with a six off Rajmohan Muthaiah, ending unbeaten on 37 off 17 alongside Govardhan, whose 36 not out anchored the chase.
